correctness.rationale: For q=t^h (t a prime power >=3, h>=2), the F_t-linear additive map s↦s^t-ms has kernel of dimension 0 or 1; every nonempty affine section of YZ^(t-1)=X^t has 1 or t rational points. The t-secant point sets are exactly cosets of one-dimensional F_t-subspaces. q+1 points and line capacity t require at least q/t+1 lines, attained by a parallel class plus Z=0. At equality, >=2 lines through infinity or a submaximal affine secant leave >=t-2 uncovered affine points even after the at-most-one contribution from the infinity line, hence exactly one infinity-line and all remaining maximal secants. When h=2, two nonparallel secants force each further secant to intersect their union, leaving at most t^2-t+2 < t^2 total affine points after infinity line: impossible. There are t+1 affine directions and t^2+1 infinity-lines, hence (t+1)(t^2+1) optimal covers. For h>=3, replacing the t u-direction cosets inside a 2-dimensional F_t-subspace by its v-direction cosets switches a parallel spread to a genuinely two-direction spread without changing cover size. Finite F_9 independent enumeration of the twelve maximal three-secants gives exactly four affine partitions and 40 optimal covers, corroborating h=2 but not proving infinite claims.
